title: Intel Accelerators Ecosystem: An SoC-Oriented Perspective : Industry Product
problem: Hyperscale datacenters face exponential compute demands amid Dennard scaling limits, with significant CPU resources consumed by common datacenter functions across multiple services (datacenter taxes).
motivation: Specialized on-chip accelerators can reduce datacenter taxes and efficiently accelerate data-intensive workloads essential to hyperscale services.
method: Because hyperscale datacenters waste CPU resources on common tasks, Intel embeds three specialized accelerators directly into its datacenter CPUs: one optimized for data movement, one for in-memory analytics, and one for workload distribution. To make this practical, these accelerators connect to the main CPU via an efficient on-chip pathway, and all three are controlled through a single unified programming interface so engineers don't need to learn three separate systems. The architecture also virtualizes the accelerators, allowing multiple applications to safely share them simultaneously.
key_novelty: The key innovation is building multiple accelerators into a single chip as a unified, virtualized ecosystem with shared programming abstractions, designed for production datacenter deployment.
contributions: Three new specialized on-chip accelerators: DSA, IAA, and DLB with detailed microarchitectures and software stacks
SoC-level features enabling efficient CPU-accelerator interaction and transparent virtualization
Comprehensive hardware/software ecosystem for easy programming and scalable deployment
Demonstration of significant datacenter tax reduction with minimal application effort

metrics.other: datacenter tax reduction, acceleration of data-intensive applications
